drivers.text: AWS sales growth reflects higher customer usage, partly offset by pricing changes tied to long-term customer contracts; AWS operating income rose on higher sales, partly offset by technology infrastructure spend supporting AWS growth.
AWS operating income increase: primarily higher sales, partially offset by infrastructure investments to support AWS growth.
Technology and infrastructure costs rose mainly from higher infrastructure spending including depreciation and amortization.
Free cash flow turned to a trailing-twelve-month outflow because purchases of property and equipment (net of proceeds and incentives) rose by $94.8 billion YoY, mainly AI investment.
Prime Day timing shifted into Q2 in 2026 (all in Q3 in 2025); management says Q3 growth would have been about 400 bps higher excluding the shift.

gaps: rpo_next_12m_pct: not found in AMZN 10-Q; the 10-Q gives only total ($578B) and weighted-average life 6.1 years.
